av_event.line_text: Gemma: Right. That's a long gap, you want to watch that. I see CVs every week, and if there's a year with nothing on it, that's the first thing I look at. I'm not saying it's fair. It's just what happens.
av_event.what: While Gemma is talking about the gap on the CV, Bethany's small smile drops. Her eyes go down and to the side, away from the screen, her lips press together, and her shoulders rise and fall in a slow, audible breath out before she looks back up at the camera.

text:
A: Hi. Gemma. Last one, I think.
B: Hi. Yeah, I think so. I'm Bethany.
A: Right. Go on, then, what do you do?
B: Erm, I'm looking for work at the moment. I did a packing job on a food line, but it was seasonal, so it finished. And I volunteer at a hospice charity shop, two mornings a week.
A: Packing. How long ago did it finish?
B: Erm... just over a year.
A: Right. That's a long gap, you want to watch that. I see CVs every week, and if there's a year with nothing on it, that's the first thing I look at. I'm not saying it's fair. It's just what happens.
B: No, I know. I've put the charity shop on it. And I did a customer service course online, a Level 2.
A: That's something. What were you like on the line?
B: I was alright, I think. I never called in sick. And I always checked the labels twice, 'cause if they're wrong the whole pallet comes back.
A: That's better than half my lot. Honestly, you'd be amazed. I've got pickers who ring in sick 'cause it's raining. You turn up and you check your labels, you'd get a job at mine tomorrow. Well, if you lived nearer. Where are you?
B: Bridgwater. In Somerset.
A: Long way from Huntingdon.
B: Yeah. Sorry.
A: Don't be sorry. There's warehouses all down the M5, isn't there.
B: My boyfriend works at one. Kieran. He drives a forklift.
A: There you go, then. Get him to ask. Half my agency staff come in 'cause somebody's mate put a word in. That's how it works, yeah?
B: I hadn't really thought of that. I think I'd sort of like something quieter, though. Like a garden centre, maybe. Or a library.
A: Quiet. Yeah, a warehouse isn't quiet.
B: No. Erm, what's it like, being a manager? It sounds really hard.
A: It's alright. It's long. Fifty, sixty hours some weeks. I was in at six this morning 'cause the agency didn't send enough bodies, then I had a client on the phone screaming about peak, then a trailer that never turned up. You spend all day putting fires out. And people don't like you much, but that's the job, isn't it.
B: I'm sure they like you a bit.
A: Dunno. Never asked. Darren reckons I've got the look.
B: Oh, I talked to him. He lives near me, actually. Same town.
A: Him? He's alright. Reminded me of my dad.
B: He reminded me of my stepdad, a bit.
A: Must be the face. Is that a bird, behind you? On the wall.
B: Yeah, a robin. I drew it. I do birds mostly, and plants. There was a little egret down by the river this morning.
A: Couldn't tell you what an egret is.
B: It's like a small white heron. Sort of. They've got bright yellow feet, like they've stepped in custard.
A: Custard. Right. Put that on your CV, you'd stand out, at lea—
